body: I've not been able to do anything about this one. AFAIK it is still relevant and should be looked into if someone has the time. The test case which is marked with an xfail should still be a good canary for if this misbehaviour remains and if a change fixes it. Unassigning myself and pinging @thedrow and @auvipy for distribution. I'm going to put this in the 5.1 milestone since it's an edge case bug IIRC, and it would be nice to fix it to avoid failing to close out canvas constructs when they error.

issue.title: Frozen chain with link_error and task protocol v1
issue.body:
# Checklist * [x] I have verified that the issue exists against the `master` branch of Celery. * [x] This has already been asked to the [discussion group](https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/celery-users) first. * [x] I have read the relevant section in the [contribution guide](http://docs.celeryproject.org/en/latest/contributing.html#other-bugs) on reporting bugs. * [x] I have checked the [issues list](https://github.com/celery/celery/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3A%22Issue+Type%3A+Bug+Report%22+-label%3A%22Category%3A+Documentation%22) for similar or identical bug reports. * [x] I have checked the [pull requests list](https://github.com/celery/celery/pulls?q=is%3Apr+label%3A%22PR+Type%3A+Bugfix%22+-label%3A%22Category%3A+Documentation%22) for existing proposed fixes. * [x] I have checked the [commit log](https://github.com/celery/celery/commits/master) to find out if the bug was already fixed in the master branch. * [x] I have included all related issues and possible duplicate issues in this issue (If there are none, check this box anyway). ## Mandatory Debugging Information * [x] I have included the output of ``celery -A proj report`` in the issue. (if you are not able to do this, then at least specify the Celery version affected). * [x] I have verified that the issue exists against the `master` branch of Celery. * [x] I have included the contents of ``pip freeze`` in the issue. * [x] I have included all the versions of all the external dependencies required to reproduce this bug. ## Related Issues and Possible Duplicates #### Possible Duplicates On IRC, the_drow mentioned it might be related to #6441. ## Environment & Settings **Celery version**: 5.1.0b1 (singularity) # Steps to Reproduce ### Python Packages
pip freeze Output:

``` $> pip freeze amqp==5.0.6 billiard==3.6.4.0 -e git+git@github.com:celery/celery.git@8ebcce1523d79039f23da748f00bec465951de2a#egg=celery click==7.1.2 click-didyoumean==0.0.3 click-plugins==1.1.1 click-repl==0.1.6 kombu==5.1.0b1 prompt-toolkit==3.0.18 pytz==2021.1 six==1.15.0 vine==5.0.0 wcwidth==0.2.5 ```

## Minimally Reproducible Test Case This minimal test case only requires Celery, and doesn't need to have anything else installed or running. ```python import sys from celery import Celery from celery.canvas import Signature, chain from celery.signals import before_task_publish app = Celery('tasks', broker='pyamqp://guest@localhost//') app.conf.task_protocol = 1 t1 = Signature('task1') t2 = Signature('task2') t3 = Signature('task3') c = chain(t1, t2) c.link_error(t3) c.freeze() @before_task_publish.connect def func(body, *args, **kwargs): print('--- Task body ---') print(body) callbacks = body['callbacks'] print(f'--- {len(callbacks)} callbacks ---') for callback in callbacks: print(f'\t{callback}') sys.exit() c.apply_async() ``` # Expected Behavior `body.callbacks` should be a list of one entry. This minimal test case: * configures celery to use task protocol version 1 * creates a chain * calls `chain.link_error()` * calls `chain.freeze()`. The field `callbacks` of the message body sent to rabbitmq should be a list of one element: the chain we want to call. # Actual Behavior `body.callbacks` is a list of two entries. The first element is the chain with options, the second without options. First entry: ``` {'task': 'task2', 'args': (), 'kwargs': {}, 'options': {'task_id': '8b6dec14-4086-4340-b8c6-1134775f8fb4', 'reply_to': '02d66300-1bee-3ebb-8b5c-9c7c97a58ffe'}, 'subtask_type': None, 'immutable': False, 'chord_size': None} ``` Second entry: ``` task2() ``` The problem only happens when both `.link_error()` and `.freeze()` are called, and when task protocol version 1 is used: * [ERROR] if `.link_error()` and `.freeze()` are called, `callbacks` is a list of two elements (this is the test case) * [OK] if `.link_error()` is not called, and `.freeze()` is called, `callbacks` is a list of one element * [OK] if `.link_error()` is called, and `.freeze()` is not called, `callbacks` is a list of one element * [OK] when task protocol is left by default (version 2), when `.link_error()` and `.freeze()` are both called, then `body[2]['chain']` is a list of one element. The problem has been introduced by ba2dec7956782 : before this commit, `callbacks` was always a list of one element. Do you have any idea what causes the problem, and what I can do to prevent the tasks from being duplicated? Thanks,

issue.title: fix: Preserve call/errbacks of replaced tasks
issue.body:
## Description

This change fixes the handling of callbacks and errbacks on tasks which get replaced to
ensure they get called as expected if the replacement signature succeeds or fails.

Fixes #6441
